small_guidance:
- The post-conv fused kernel is already cheap; runtime is dominated by `nn.ConvTranspose3d`. Tuning BLOCK_C/num_warps on the existing kernel will not move fast_p meaningfully. If staying small, at least also fuse the MaxPool3d into the same kernel pass (one program per (n, pooled-spatial) doing the 2×2×2 max over the conv output before softmax), eliminating a full read/write of the post-conv tensor.
- Fold the per-channel `subtract` parameter pre-load into shared/registers once per program; current code is fine but ensure `num_warps=2` since C=16 makes BLOCK_C=16 (single warp's worth of lanes) — fewer warps reduces launch overhead.
large_guidance:
- Replace `nn.ConvTranspose3d` with a custom Triton scatter-add kernel: one program per (N, IC-tile, input-spatial-tile) computing the outer product `input[n,ic,d,h,w] * weight[ic,oc,kd,kh,kw]` and scatter-adding into the strided output grid at `(d*stride - pad + kd, ...)`. This is the dominant op (~90% of runtime) and the only high-headroom move.
- Better: fuse ConvTranspose3d → MaxPool3d → softmax → subtract → swish → channel-max into a single persistent kernel keyed on the *final* output spatial coordinate. Since pool_stride=2 and conv stride=2 give a deterministic mapping from output voxel back to a small input receptive field, each program can accumulate the full 16-channel vector for its 2×2×2 post-conv window directly from input+weight, then do softmax/sub/swish/max in registers — never materializing the intermediate (128,16,32,64,64) tensor.
- If full fusion is too complex, at minimum write a custom transposed-conv kernel in channels-last layout and fuse bias + pool into its epilogue; leave the existing post kernel as-is.
